title: Character splay: a headline that opens in 3D from its centre
summary: A display headline split after `document.fonts.ready` by `SplitText.create` (lines, words, chars; `aria: 'auto'`, so the h1 keeps one accessible name; `autoSplit` re-splits when its width changes) whose characters each take one weight, `(distance from the headline's centre ÷ half the widest line)^1.6`, scaled into six channels: `x` outward `.28 × half`, `y` down `.8 ×` line height so each line bends into an arc, `z` forward `.7 × half`, `rotateY` `60°` towards its own side, `rotateX` `36°` by row and `rotate` `24°` along the arc, under a perspective of `2.6 × half` on each line centred on it; one timeline built in `onSplit`, scrubbed (`ease: none`) across a `230svh` hero's sticky stage, clears every inline transform at progress 0 so the heading returns to plain set text; a closing heading plays the same offsets once, open to shut, `1.2 s` expo-out at `center bottom`; reduced motion splits nothing, releases the hero to one screen and fades it to `.12` as it leaves, static only releases it
variants: scrubbed open as the hero leaves, from a sticky stage (this, default)
played once, open to shut, when a heading's centre reaches the viewport bottom: the same targets as a `gsap.from`, 1.2 s expo-out (the closing heading here; the source's own use)
per word instead of per headline: measure each word's centre and half width, so every word fans from its own middle like a deck
split-text-masked-reveal for a reading-weight reveal of lines; this is for one display line that should come apart
